screen.title: Environment check
screen.intro: Checking whether this computer is ready. Every item ends as Pass / Warning / Blocked; blocked items come with a way to fix them.
screen.runFailed: The environment check did not complete. Please try again.
screen.diagnoseHint: Analyses the results for common causes and lists the steps to fix them.
screen.diagnoseNote: These findings are based on the results of this environment check.

summary.pass: All {{total}} checks passed. You can move on.
summary.warn: Done: {{pass}} passed, {{warn}} warning(s). Warnings do not block you, but they are worth a look.
summary.fail: Done: {{fail}} blocked, {{warn}} warning(s), {{pass}} passed. Please deal with the blocked items first.
summary.continueAnyway: I understand some items are blocked; continue anyway (the next step installs what is missing)
summary.continueAnywayHint: Skipping is only offered when every blocked item can be fixed by installing something; other blockers must be resolved first.

os.title: Operating system
os.too_old: Operating system version {{version}} is below the minimum; some components may not install
os.unknown: Could not identify the operating system version; the other checks continue

node.title: Node.js
node.missing: Node.js was not found. Both Codex CLI and Claude Code need it
node.too_old: The installed Node.js {{version}} is too old; please upgrade to a recent long-term-support (LTS) release
node.not_on_path: Node.js is installed ({{path}}) but this terminal cannot see it yet — usually because no new terminal was opened after installing
node.broken: Node.js was found ({{path}}) but it does not run properly (node --version failed). Please reinstall Node.js and check again

instructions.not_on_path:
Node.js is installed; the current terminal simply has not picked up the new PATH yet:
1. Close every terminal window completely (Windows: Command Prompt, PowerShell, Windows Terminal; macOS: Terminal, iTerm, …).
2. On Windows, if you just installed Node.js, sign out and back in once.
3. Open a fresh terminal and type node --version — a version number means it works.
4. Come back here and click “Re-check”.

npm.title: npm
npm.missing: npm was not found. It ships with Node.js — install or reinstall Node.js first
npm.broken: npm was found ({{path}}) but it does not run properly (npm --version failed). Please reinstall Node.js and check again

tool.missing: {{tool}} was not found; the next step can install it for you
tool.not_on_path: {{tool}} is installed at {{path}} but this terminal cannot see it yet — usually because no new terminal was opened after installing
tool.broken: {{tool}} was found ({{path}}) but it does not run properly (the version command failed). Please reinstall it and check again
tool.not_configured: The current preset has no entry for the tool {{toolId}}; the check was skipped

instructions.not_on_path:
{{tool}} is already installed; the terminal just has not picked up the new PATH yet:
1. Close every terminal window completely.
2. Open a fresh terminal and type {{tool}} --version — a version number means it works.
3. If the command is still not found, make sure the folder {{dir}} is on your PATH (Windows: Settings → System → About → Advanced system settings → Environment Variables; macOS: check ~/.zshrc or ~/.zprofile). Editing environment variables is something you do yourself — this tool never changes them.
4. Come back here and click “Re-check”.

check.internal_error: This check did not complete. Please try again; if it keeps happening, send the diagnostic report to support

cc_switch.title: CC Switch
cc_switch.missing: CC Switch was not found; the next step can download it for you
cc_switch.data_only: Found the CC Switch data folder ({{dataDir}}) but not the app itself — it may have been uninstalled or moved. Please reinstall it

env_vars.title: Environment variables
env_vars.clean: No environment variables that would interfere with the configuration
env_vars.conflicts: Found environment variables that can override the CC Switch configuration: {{names}}. Please remove them by hand as described before continuing

instructions.windows:
These variables override what you configure in CC Switch, so Codex / Claude Code may talk to the wrong address or use the wrong key. Please remove them yourself (this tool never edits your environment variables):
1. Open Settings → System → About → Advanced system settings → Environment Variables.
2. Look for {{names}} in both the “User variables” and “System variables” lists.
3. Select each one, click Delete, then click OK all the way out to save.
4. Close every terminal window and CC Switch completely, then reopen them.
5. Come back here and click “Re-check” to confirm they are gone.
instructions.macos:
These variables override what you configure in CC Switch, so Codex / Claude Code may talk to the wrong address or use the wrong key. Please remove them yourself (this tool never edits your environment variables):
1. Open Terminal and check these files one by one: ~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.zshenv, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile (for example open -e ~/.zshrc opens it in TextEdit).
2. Find the line that looks like export {{names}}=… , delete the whole line and save.
3. If the check listed launchctl as a source, run launchctl unsetenv NAME in Terminal.
4. Close every terminal window completely and open a new one.
5. Come back here and click “Re-check” to confirm they are gone.

network.mirror_only: {{target}} is not directly reachable, but a mirror is; installs will switch to it automatically
network.unreachable: {{target}} is unreachable. Please check your network or proxy settings

envVars.title: Environment variables found
envVars.intro: These variables influence which address and key Codex / Claude Code use. Values are partially hidden for safety. This tool never modifies them.
